The application stands disposed of.

1. Inter alia, learned counsel for the applicant contends that the alleged offences attributed to the applicant attracting Sections 406 and 420 of IPC out of a civil dispute between the parties and in any case, no ingredients thereof even otherwise are made out.
He would submit that both the Sections i.e. Section 406 of IPC (criminal breach of trust and Section 420 (cheating) cannot be invoked simultaneously as they are completely antithetical to each other.

sentences.text: Furthermore, he would point out that whatever alleged transaction which led to the false allegations happened in Delhi as the applicant never visited Barmer at any stage to conduct any business with the complainants/ informers in the FIR.
3. He would point out that the applicants are residents of Delhi, and in complete abuse of criminal machinery, the FIR has been registered in Barmer.
They are not aware as to what are the contents of the FIR.
The case of the applicants is that they do not even know the complainants and never met them and never carried out any business with them and it could well be a case of mistaken identity.
4. He would submit that the applicants apprehend that in case they travel to Barmer which is about 13 hours from Delhi by road being about 800 kilometres.
they are fearful that enroute, when they enter Rajasthan, they may be arrested on the basis of the false allegations levelled in the FIR.
5. On being questioned as to what is their apprehension of arrest, they This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 09/08/2025 at 00:17:20 would submit that they have been served two separate notices in Delhi, both dated 22.07.2025, one under Section 35(3) of the BNSS, 2023 and other under Section 94(1)(2)(3).
6.

Learned counsel would submit that the applicants are law abiding citizens and have no intention to evade the process of law and are willing to abide by any condition that may be imposed by this Court.
7. Issue notice.

8. Ms. Priyanka Dalal, learned APP appears on advance notice and states that the applicant ought to have made State of Rajasthan a party, since the FIR is registered in Barmer, Rajasthan and not under the territorial jurisdiction of the NCT of Delhi.

9. At her oral request, State of Rajasthan is arrayed as a party through Superintendent of Police,
Barmer.

10. Applicants shall file an amended memo of parties and also serve the newly added respondent no.
2 through the Resident Commissioner of the State of Rajasthan in Delhi, who shall transmit copy of the instant order to the Superintendent of Police, Barmer.
11.

In the meanwhile, applicant on his own volition shall contact the Station House Officer of the Police Station from where they have received the aforesaid notice and seek the next date of appearing before him.
In case they are unable to contact the SHO, they shall report at the Police Station, Barmer on 12.08.2025 at 2 PM.
Till then, no coercive steps shall be taken against them.
